title: Using Claude to make VFX *Update*
author: Equivalent-Future439
selftext:
https://reddit.com/link/1uqgk4f/video/klp0qu2q8xbh1/player

I posted earlier with just the simple water blob effect. Here is a more built version of the skill. I think it looks pretty decent. Any suggestions for improvements?

comments.author: Zerrul
comments.body: Looks awesome! What's the actual process of building special effects like this? Is it all shaders? 3d models with textures and animation?

replies.author: Equivalent-Future439
replies.body: I have a pretty large VFX texture/masks library so a lot of the effects are derived from that. I do have claude building shaders based off of real life examples, and I'm having it use Wolfram MCP to check the math. I think this particular shader referencing BinBun's water asset pack that I bought, and also a tutorial on how to build the physics around the water blob. It's mostly referencing material available online on how to certain techniques, and then I have it indexed in a RAG for quick cross referencing when building effects. I've been mostly using fable so far, but I'm trying to harden it so opus can steer is similarly.

replies.author: Zerrul
replies.body: Fascinating, thank you for the write-up!

comments.author: Mammoth-Drawing-6939
comments.body: this is pretty impressive. what was the process?

replies.author: Equivalent-Future439
replies.body: Copied this comment from my previous post: I've built a stringent skill that references official Godot docs, any free tutorials and techniques online, and I'm using Genshin/Wuthering Waves, those kinds of anime games for styling reference. I'm using an extensive VFX library (free stuff on itch and other places) and some paid VFX that I have the AI also reference in terms of structure and stuff like that. It's been pretty impressive so far to be honest
